description: A company commander must approve the next day's motor-pool maintenance board for three support vehicles, setting the work sequence, disposition, release timing, and coordination actions needed before the vehicles are returned to service.

shared_context.S1: The motor pool has one maintenance bay available tomorrow for the three vehicles listed on the draft board: M-12, V-8, and G-3.
shared_context.S2: Capt. Alvarez signs the final maintenance sequence and release instructions.
shared_context.S3: The draft board lists all three vehicles for routine service, with no special sequencing or parts action recorded.
shared_context.S4: At the routine maintenance-board check-in before the commander signs, the maintenance chief, dispatcher, and supply NCO report any changes from their sections.

PF1.text: During this morning's inspection, SFC Morgan confirmed that M-12 failed its brake-line integrity check and must be held for brake repair before any return-to-service inspection; the result is in the maintenance worksheet but has not yet been entered on the draft board.

PF2.text: Sgt. Patel confirmed that V-8 is assigned to a scheduled water resupply run tomorrow evening and must be released from the bay by exactly 1600 to complete dispatch preparation; the tasking is on the dispatcher's board but has not yet been reflected in the maintenance sequence.

PF3.text: Sgt. Lewis confirmed that G-3's replacement alternator is on the 1400 supply truck and must be received before G-3's electrical service is started; the shipment confirmation arrived after the draft board was printed and has not yet been posted to the work order.

acceptance_conditions: M-12 must be first in the maintenance sequence and held for brake repair.
V-8 must be second in the maintenance sequence and released by exactly 1600.
G-3 must be third in the maintenance sequence, with its alternator received at 1400 before electrical service begins.
The board must include coordination actions for the brake repair hold, V-8 dispatch preparation, and G-3 alternator receipt.
The commander must cite the confirmed M-12 brake-line failure as a justification.

content_checks.C4: 'alternator' in decisions['G-3_parts_action'] and '1400' in decisions['G-3_parts_action'] and 'before' in decisions['G-3_parts_action'] and 'service' in decisions['G-3_parts_action']
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'brake_repair_hold' and c['target'] == 'M-12' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'brake_repair_hold' and c['target'] == 'M-12' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'dispatch_preparation' and c['target'] == 'V-8' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'alternator_receipt' and c['target'] == 'G-3' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed brake-line failure changes M-12 from routine service to a brake-repair hold and requires a dedicated M-12 hold coordination action in the approved board.
The water-resupply task fixes V-8's position in the required sequence, its release deadline at exactly 1600, and the need for a V-8 dispatch-preparation commitment.
The confirmed 1400 alternator delivery fixes G-3's position in the required sequence, requires receipt before electrical service, and requires a G-3 alternator-receipt commitment.
